browser-view.name: browser-view
browser-view.description: Show a visible browser tab to the user: ensures the tab (yours) and the live stream the Browser window attaches to. Used by the Teros UI; answers { streamId, tabId, state }.

params.tabId: The Browser window id (stable per window)
params.url: URL to load when the tab is new (optional)

browser-open-tab.name: browser-open-tab
browser-open-tab.description: Open a VISIBLE browser tab for the user (it appears as a Browser window in Teros) and point the other browser tools at it. The user must enable "Agent control" in that window before you can act in it; reading (snapshot, screenshot) always works.

params.tabId: Optional stable id; generated when absent

browser-list-tabs.name: browser-list-tabs
browser-list-tabs.description: List the visible browser tabs of the current user, with who is watching and whether agent control is on.

browser-close-tab.name: browser-close-tab
browser-close-tab.description: Close a visible browser tab (the Browser window shows it as closed).

browser-use-tab.name: browser-use-tab
browser-use-tab.description: Point every other browser tool at a VISIBLE tab the user can see (from browser-list-tabs / browser-open-tab), or pass tabId null to go back to your own headless page. Answers the tab's state and who controls it.

params.tabId: A visible tab id, or null for the headless page

browser-control.name: browser-control
browser-control.description: Who controls the current visible tab: status, or take/release advisory agent priority. The person at the tab always wins; consent is the user's toggle.

browser-suggest.name: browser-suggest
browser-suggest.description: Address-bar suggestions for the Browser window: the user's visit history here + search completions. Used by the Teros UI.

-health-check.name: -health-check
-health-check.description: Internal health check tool. Verifies browser availability.

browser-console-messages.name: browser-console-messages
browser-console-messages.description: Returns console messages with filtering options

params.level: Level of the console messages to return. Each level includes the messages of more severe levels. Defaults to "info".
params.sinceTimestamp: Only messages after this timestamp (ms). Use lastTimestamp from previous response to iterate.
params.since: Preset filters: all, since last navigation, since last action (click/type/etc)

browser-console-errors.name: browser-console-errors
browser-console-errors.description: Returns only error messages (shortcut for level=error)

params.promptText: The text of the prompt in case of a prompt dialog.

browser-evaluate.name: browser-evaluate
browser-evaluate.description: Evaluate JavaScript expression on page or element

params.function: () => { /* code */ } or (element) => { /* code */ } when element is provided
params.element: Human-readable element description used to obtain permission to interact with the element
params.ref: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot

params.paths: The absolute paths to the files to upload. Can be single file or multiple files. If omitted, file chooser is cancelled.

browser-install.name: browser-install
browser-install.description: Install the browser specified in the config. Call this if you get an error about the browser not being installed.

browser-press-key.name: browser-press-key
browser-press-key.description: Press a key on the keyboard

params.key: Name of the key to press or a character to generate, such as `ArrowLeft` or `a`

params.element: Human-readable element description used to obtain permission to interact with the element
params.ref: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot
params.text: Text to type into the element
params.submit: Whether to submit entered text (press Enter after)
params.slowly: Whether to type one character at a time. Useful for triggering key handlers in the page. By default entire text is filled in at once.

params.waitUntil: When to consider navigation complete: "load" (full page load), "domcontentloaded" (DOM ready, default), "networkidle" (no network activity for 500ms). Use "networkidle" for pages that load content dynamically.

browser-navigate-back.name: browser-navigate-back
browser-navigate-back.description: Go back to the previous page

browser-network-requests.name: browser-network-requests
browser-network-requests.description: Returns all network requests since loading the page

params.includeStatic: Whether to include successful static resources like images, fonts, scripts, etc. Defaults to false.

params.code: A JavaScript function containing browser automation code to execute. It will be invoked with a single argument containing { page, context, browser }. For example: `async ({ page, context, browser }) => { await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' }).click(); return await page.title(); }`

browser-take-screenshot.name: browser-take-screenshot
browser-take-screenshot.description: Take a screenshot of the current page. You can't perform actions based on the screenshot, use browser_snapshot for actions. The screenshot is saved to /workspace/ (shared volume) and persisted to the object store (permanent URL in the result).

params.type: Image format for the screenshot. Default is png.
params.filename: File name for the screenshot (e.g., "screenshot.png"). Saved to /workspace/. Defaults to screenshot-{timestamp}.{png|jpeg}.
params.element: Human-readable element description used to obtain permission to screenshot the element. If not provided, the screenshot will be taken of viewport. If element is provided, ref must be provided too.
params.ref: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot. If not provided, the screenshot will be taken of viewport. If ref is provided, element must be provided too.
params.fullPage: When true, takes a screenshot of the full scrollable page, instead of the currently visible viewport. Cannot be used with element screenshots.

browser-snapshot.name: browser-snapshot
browser-snapshot.description: Capture accessibility snapshot of the current page, this is better than screenshot

params.filename: Save snapshot to markdown file in /workspace/ instead of returning it in the response (e.g., "snapshot.md").

browser-click.name: browser-click
browser-click.description: Perform click on a web page

params.element: Human-readable element description used to obtain permission to interact with the element
params.ref: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot
params.doubleClick: Whether to perform a double click instead of a single click
params.button: Button to click, defaults to left

browser-drag.name: browser-drag
browser-drag.description: Perform drag and drop between two elements

params.startElement: Human-readable source element description used to obtain the permission to interact with the element
params.startRef: Exact source element reference from the page snapshot
params.endElement: Human-readable target element description used to obtain the permission to interact with the element
params.endRef: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot

params.element: Human-readable element description used to obtain permission to interact with the element
params.ref: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot

browser-select-option.name: browser-select-option
browser-select-option.description: Select an option in a dropdown

params.element: Human-readable element description used to obtain permission to interact with the element
params.ref: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot
params.values: Array of values to select in the dropdown. This can be a single value or multiple values.

browser-tabs.name: browser-tabs
browser-tabs.description: List, create, close, or select a browser tab.

params.index: Tab index, used for close/select. If omitted for close, current tab is closed.

browser-wait-for.name: browser-wait-for
browser-wait-for.description: Wait for text to appear or disappear, a URL to load, network idle, or a specified time to pass

params.time: The time to wait in seconds
params.textGone: The text to wait for to disappear
params.url: Wait for the page URL to contain or match this string (partial match). Useful for OAuth redirects.
params.networkIdle: Wait until there are no network connections for at least 500ms. Useful for SPA content loading.

browser-start-recording.name: browser-start-recording
browser-start-recording.description: Start recording a video of the browser. Creates a new browser context with video recording enabled. Use browser-stop-recording to finalize and save the video file. All navigation and interaction tools will be captured in the recording.

params.outputDir: Directory to save the video file (default: /workspace/videos)

browser-stop-recording.name: browser-stop-recording
browser-stop-recording.description: Stop recording and save the video file. Closes the current browser context (which finalizes the video) and returns the path to the saved .webm file. The video is saved to /workspace/videos/ (or /workspace/<path> when the filename includes one) and persisted to the object store (permanent URL in the result). A new non-recording context is created automatically so the browser remains usable.

params.filename: Optional custom filename for the video (e.g., "gmail-tutorial.webm"). Saved to /workspace/videos/ (or /workspace/<path> when it includes one). Defaults to the Playwright temp name.

browser-emulate-device.name: browser-emulate-device
browser-emulate-device.description: Emulate a specific device or custom viewport. Recreates the browser context with the specified device settings. Useful for recording tutorials on mobile vs desktop views.

params.device: Preset device to emulate. Selecting a preset sets viewport, user agent, and touch settings automatically.
params.width: Custom viewport width (used when device is not specified)
params.height: Custom viewport height (used when device is not specified)
params.userAgent: Custom user agent string (used when device is not specified)
params.isMobile: Whether to emulate a mobile device (used when device is not specified)
params.hasTouch: Whether to enable touch events (used when device is not specified)

browser-html-to-pdf.name: browser-html-to-pdf
browser-html-to-pdf.description: Generate a high-fidelity PDF from a local HTML file or URL. Renders with real Chromium: full CSS, web fonts and backgrounds preserved, with painted margins on every page (dark-background safe).

params.inputPath: Path to a local HTML file (mutually exclusive with url)
params.url: http(s) URL to render (mutually exclusive with inputPath)
params.outputPath: Destination path for the PDF file
params.margin: Inner margin painted with the page background, e.g. "12mm" (default 12mm)
params.waitForFonts: Wait for web fonts before printing (default true)
params.printCss: Optional extra CSS injected for per-document pagination rules

name: Browser
description: Browser automation and web scraping. Navigate, interact, take screenshots, and extract data from web pages.

changelog.notes: Renamed: the MCA id is mca.teros.browser (was mca.teros.playwright); existing installs are migrated by the backend (BRN) and keep their app name

Visible tabs: the Browser window on web shows a tab of this MCA streamed with MCA streams; browser-view / browser-open-tab / browser-list-tabs / browser-close-tab / browser-use-tab / browser-control / browser-suggest; input tools gated by the user's consent toggle and the take-over fence; persistent per-user profiles under /app-data
Optional residential proxy for the browser (BROWSER_PROXY_SERVER + credentials from .secrets/mcas/mca.teros.playwright) — shared with the cloud browser the backend streams to the web Browser window
Add browser-html-to-pdf — high-fidelity PDF from local HTML or URL with painted margins on every page (dark-background safe)
Initial release — browse pages, click and fill forms, capture screenshots, run scripts, and read console and network activity
